newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore physical gas oil trades at record $29.70.
newsitem.headline: Singapore physical gas oil trades at record $29.70.

text.p: A European major oil company on Wednesday sold 220,000 barrels of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil to a US trader at a five-year record of $29.70 a barrel for October 17-21 lifting, free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis, traders said.
The previous record for a traded physical gas oil cargo was seen in February at $27.90 per barrel, fob Singapore, when a Swiss trader bought the cargo, traders said.
They said the spike in physical and swaps gas oil prices was particularly due to high Brent crude and gas oil futures prices on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
IPE Brent followed through on its overnight gains to rise another 29 cents a barrel to $23.35, while gas oil gained $3.75 a tonne to $239.50.
October swaps opened about $1.50 a barrel over Tuesdsay, and rallied another 50 cents to trade as high as $29.05 a barrel.
Physical gas oil has been poised to trade at a post Gulf War high since mid-September on tensions in the Gulf and as the market enters a peak demand period.
Traders said the high prices in Europe has seen the Asian market trying to play catch up over the past few months.
They said the record high level, which was finally traded today, reflected low stocks in the west, lesser exports from the Middle East and latent demand from China.
Traders also cited Indonesia's higher demand, amid the shutdown of two refineries in September and October/November, as another reason for the continued strength in gas oil prices.
The market's underlying strength was seen when it shrugged off India's cancellation of its tender for November delivery, after two months of reduced buying.
